headline: Last session: Sensex fell 289 points amid inflation concerns, though markets extended weekly gains

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 16 November.

why: Sensex fell 289 points in the last session as inflation concerns weighed on investor sentiment.
Indian stock markets extended their rally for the third consecutive week despite global headwinds.
Earlier sessions benefited from strong foreign fund inflows and lower crude oil prices.
PSU Banks emerged as top sectoral gainers during the weekly market wrap.
whatHappening: Yes Bank has moved the Supreme Court seeking a review of an order regarding the write-off of Rs 8,415 crore AT-1 bonds.
RHI Magnesita reported a 62% jump in Q2 net profit to over Rs 62 crore.
NIFTY50 and SENSEX registered a third straight week of gains overall.
Gold returns over the past year stood at 7.7%, lower than many fixed deposit rates.
summary: In the last trading session, Sensex fell 289 points as inflation concerns weighed on investor confidence. Despite Friday's decline, Indian markets achieved their third straight week of gains, supported by PSU banks and foreign fund inflows earlier in the week. Key corporate highlights include Yes Bank appealing an AT-1 bond write-off order in the Supreme Court and RHI Magnesita reporting a 62% rise in Q2 net profit.
